source_documents.title: The role of higher excited states in the photophysics and photochemistry of a BODIPY–phenol derivative

conditions_studied: solution, excitation at 495, 335 and 272 nm (fluorescence upconversion, transient absorption)

reference_evidence_units.quote: The photodynamics of 1 is strongly wavelength dependent. Visible excitation leads to rapid internal conversion to the S1 state, and results in green fluorescence without detectable photochemistry.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Normal S1 BODIPY emission near 510-530 nm.

reference_evidence_units.quote: In contrast, UV excitation opens additional pathways, giving rise to weak high-energy fluorescence and ultrafast deamination.

The anomalous emission originates from the lowest electronic state of the third absorption band with phenyl-to-BODIPY CT character (CTPH-BP), where partial population trapping occurs due to suppression of internal conversion by the relatively large interband energy gap and restricted access to conical intersections.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Upper CT state is trapped by a large interband gap and restricted access to conical intersections.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Therefore, this emission from a high-lying excited state is better viewed as an intraband extension rather than a strict violation of Kasha’s rule.

Our simulations show that photodeamination proceeds through higher CT states with BODIPY-to-phenyl character and involves rapid C–N bond cleavage occurring before intramolecular vibrational energy redistribution.
reference_evidence_units.statement: Photochemistry runs through other upper CT states.

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Restricted access to conical intersections (RACI, RIM family) is the second reason given for the population trapping; intrinsic, from simulations.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The emitting upper state has phenyl-to-BODIPY CT character.

reference_mechanisms.label: RADIATIVE_RATE_STATE_BALANCE
reference_mechanisms.rationale: The weak high-energy emission survives because a large interband energy gap slows internal conversion from the upper CT state.

out_of_pool: SOKR_ANTI_KASHA: weak 350-400 nm emission from an upper CT state (the paper calls it an intraband extension rather than a strict Kasha violation) (E02, E03, E04)
PHOTOCHEMISTRY: UV photo-deamination to a quinone methide through higher CT states (E02, E05)

basis: structure recognition of Scheme 1 (main text p2): meso 4-hydroxy-3-(dimethylammoniomethyl)phenyl tetramethyl BODIPY chloride, with its quinone-methide and solvent-adduct products
photoelimination of N(CH3)2H+Cl- described in the text; the paper calls the species 1+
